text:
anya_ml: Quick sync — I ran a tiny shadow run for a new speculative decode variant I'm prototyping (internal name: shadowbeam). Wanted to share raw notes before I formalize the eval.

kevin_eng: nice. short summary first? numbers + config

anya_ml: TL;DR: on llama3-12b int4 (our quant recipe Q2b) -> token throughput ~1.8-2.0x vs baseline decode, p95 latency down ~20-30ms for 512-token tails. Quality: our ROUGE-like QA pass rate drops ~0.6-1.1% absolute on the summarize suite, but heuristics-only prompts are fine.

sasha_research: What's shadowbeam doing differently vs current spec-prefetch? is it two-stage sampling, or a different KV scheduling?

anya_ml: It's a hybrid: speculative short-beam proposals (k=4 fast logits with temperature 0.7) used to prefill KV for likely continuations + a micro-latebinding check that rejects low-prob tails. Implementation is intentionally cheap: single-threaded CPU soft proposals + GPU-prefetch of KV.

kevin_eng: config paste pls

anya_ml: ```
model: llama3-12b-qt-q2b
speculative: {
  proposer: beam_k4_temp0.7_cpu_fast
  accept_threshold: 0.28
  max_prefill_tokens: 32
}
batching: dynamic, max_batch=48
quant: int4 (per-channel, symmetric)
metrics: latency_ms, tokens_per_s, prompt_eval.pass_rate
``` 

ciara_bot: quick note — this thread triggered a perf alert: shadow runs must not affect prod runtime caches.

jordan_ops: how did you simulate traffic? prefix length distribution? KV-hit patterns matter.

anya_ml: Simulated from 12k production-like traces: 60% short (<128), 30% mid (128-512), 10% long (>512). We replayed stochastic sampling with user think-time and 5% multi-turn continuation. Also included cold-cache runs to stress KV warmup.

sasha_research: And eval set? holdouts?

anya_ml: For quality: 10k prompts across 3 cohorts (summarize 4k, code 3k, chit-chat+instr 3k). Stratified by length. We ran paired A/B on same seeds for 5k matched pairs; computed bootstrap CIs (n=10k resamples). Observed small but consistent decrease on summarize subset (0.6% abs, 95% CI 0.4-0.9%). p-value ~0.007 by paired t-test.

kevin_eng: 0.6% absolute might be acceptable given perf win, but depends on customer SLAs. Any visible systematic biases (e.g., truncation of rare entities, hallucination)?

anya_ml: Good call. Manual triage on 200 failures: ~55% were factual-inference errors (dates/names swapped), 30% were style-level (shortened summaries losing nuance), remainder were sampling variance. Most failures correlated with long-prefix contexts that the proposer erroneously favored.

jordan_ops: That suggests proposer threshold tuning. Can we do an adaptive threshold by prefix-length or top-token entropy?

anya_ml: I already tried linear decay of accept_threshold with prefix_length (threshold = base - 0.0006 * prefix_len). That recovered ~0.35% of the drop, at cost of 6% perf loss on long contexts.

sasha_research: What about an experiment: hybrid canary where we enable shadowbeam for 20% traffic but only on short/mid (<256) prefixes. If we see no regression in prod metrics for 2 days, extend to mid.

kevin_eng: Sounds sensible. Also request: run repeat on llama3-70b-qt (same quant recipe) — large models shift distribution and proposer error rates might change.

anya_ml: Agreed. My quick 2k sample on 70b int4 showed perf ~1.6x (less headroom), quality drop similar magnitude but noisier because sample small. I'll scale to 20k.

ciara_bot: ops checklist reminder: must not change rollout config for Dedicated customers without SRE signoff.

jordan_ops: For rollout plan: canary 1% (short prefixes only) -> 20% short+mid for 48h -> 5% long shadow read-only for 24h -> full conditional rollout. Also add automatic fallback to baseline model if error-rate > 1.5x baseline.

anya_ml: Implementation note: KV prefill is non-idempotent in current runtime; I added a deterministic hash to proposer seeds so A/B is reproducible. Logs below from a single session (truncated):

```
[1700ms] req start id=abcd
[1706ms] proposer(k4) returned candidates in 5ms
[1712ms] gpu prefill KV tokens=24 time=9ms
[1730ms] decode accept/reject step time=18ms accept=true
[1789ms] response tokens=128 total_ms=89 p95=112
```

kevin_eng: Nice. Implementation question: is proposer on CPU threading stealing cores from schedulers? need to isolate.

anya_ml: It's pinned to nic-1 isolated cores in the bench; production integration will need a dedicated cpu-pool for proposers or run in lightweight wasm worker. Profiling shows proposer median CPU 12% on 4-core test VM.

sasha_research: Longer-term thought: we should add a small offline scorer that compares proposer top-1 to final top-1 distribution and reports KL divergence by prefix-length. That gives an early reg signal without full quality eval.

anya_ml: Good idea — I computed a quick KL per-length bucket; long prefixes had KL ~0.18 vs 0.05 for short, which tracks the QA failures.

jordan_ops: Action items:
- anya: run 70b 20k A/B, stratified. report 48h.
- kevin: help instrument KL and entropy dashboards by prefix bucket.
- sasha: assemble 500 manual failure cases for triage and write short-quality-issue playbook.
- ops: prepare canary config with fallback and CPU isolation.

kevin_eng: I'll add perf/kl panels to Console and wire an alert when KL_long > 0.12 or summarize-pass_rate drops >0.5%.

ciara_bot: noted. creating ticket INF-ml-shadowbeam-canary

anya_ml: Thanks all — I'll post the 70b numbers here when done. If anyone sees weirdness in prod logs attributed to this thread, ping me directly. :pray:

sasha_research: One more: let's add a regression check that measures hallucination label (binary) via our classifier; we care about that more than ROUGE sometimes.

anya_ml: Will add. Expected timeline: 70b runs done EOD + aggregated report tomorrow AM.
